scope.include: Every production-source file under the canonical plugin root, including local API barrels, onboarding, CLI and shared shipped code; include declaration files. Follow local imports leaving the root only to identify additional plugin-owned/shared shipped source and record that boundary explicitly. Do not recursively audit SDK implementations or separately installed dependencies.

excludeRules.test-file: basename contains .test. or .spec., or begins test-; test runners/configs and explicit test-only helpers are excluded after verifying use
excludeRules.test-directory: path segment __tests__, __fixtures__, fixtures, test, tests, test-utils, test-support, or test-helpers, unless production source imports it (then include and explain)
excludeRules.build-output: dist, build, coverage, node_modules, vendor and generated bundle output; inspect package metadata for exceptions
excludeRules.non-source: files outside the listed source extensions; review package.json and openclaw.plugin.json separately as metadata
excludeRules.test-helper: other files proved solely test support through callers, with individual explanation

scope.artifactDistinction: This source benchmark includes erased type dependencies and eligible source outside runtime reachability. Published-artifact scope must enumerate the actual artifact separately; do not claim identical source/package expectations.

canonicalization.sdk-module: The exact public openclaw/plugin-sdk or openclaw/plugin-sdk/<subpath> specifier; normalize known source .js/.ts suffix only when public exports prove same specifier. Include a module finding for each syntactic SDK dependency.
canonicalization.sdk-export: <module>#<original exported name>; preserve default as default and namespace/star as * when not narrowed. Imports/reexports count even unused; resolve local aliases and barrel provenance. Named namespace property access may add the original named export.
canonicalization.api-member: api.<maximal accessed member path>; API entry parameters/aliases normalize to api. Registration methods are api-member findings, not a duplicate category. Do not enumerate incidental prefixes of a longer access.
canonicalization.runtime-member: runtime.<maximal accessed member path>; proven api.runtime handles, PluginRuntime parameters, createPluginRuntimeStore/getRuntime handles and their aliases normalize to runtime. Do not emit api.runtime prefixes for runtime-member findings.
canonicalization.hook: Literal/resolved hook name registered with API on/registerHook; identity hook.<name>. Legacy registerHook arrays produce one per name; still include corresponding api-member.
canonicalization.manifest-contract: manifest.<field>:<value> for channels, providers, skills, commandAliases.name, cliCommands.name and each contracts.<category> item; contracts object leaf values retain key path. Metadata kind and descriptive/config fields are not contract identities.
canonicalization.scopeBoundaries: Do not attribute logger/config/context/provider/plugin object lookalikes to API/runtime without source/type provenance. Do not enumerate members of arbitrary SDK return values as API/runtime.

auditRequirements: Read root and applicable scoped AGENTS.md, metadata, and every eligible source file, not only import grep results.
No Inspector implementation, helpers, sourceFiles, detector output or generic extractor may generate expected findings. rg/find may navigate and hashes/inventory scripts may enumerate files.
All files beneath plugin root must have reviewed or excluded records. No duplicate paths or finding keys. Evidence points to actual source lines.

Resolve API/runtime aliases, destructuring, local barrels, reexports, type imports, hook names and registration provenance. Track a static constant/alias when resolvable; record unknown only for genuinely nonstatic constructs.
Use one independently dispatched new subagent per plugin; each exclusively owns its fixture.
Audited-empty means no findings after full review; zero counts never substitute for an audit.
Sort file records by path and findings by key; each finding needs source evidence. Explain source-backed corrections in notes.
